title: Tega Industries Ltd - 543413 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tega Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR17.2bn with 15% adjusted EBITDA margin, including one month of Molycop; consumables grew 36% YoY.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter consolidating Molycop, but only for June 2026 after the June 1 closing. Consolidated revenue was about INR17.2bn and adjusted EBITDA about INR2.6bn (15% margin) before INR1.9bn of one-time acquisition and integration costs. Legacy Tega consumables delivered strong growth and margin expansion, while the equipment business fell sharply on delayed customer clearances. Management stressed that one month of Molycop is too short to draw full-year conclusions, but said June was directionally ahead of acquisition expectations.

financial_highlights.value: INR1.9bn (INR1.85bn in Molycop results, per CFO)
financial_highlights.change: Prior-year one-time costs about INR0.75-0.8bn per analyst reconciliation
Income +23% YoY from INR3.72bn; EBITDA from INR0.71bn (~19%)
+3% YoY for June; described as ~30% margin in Q&A, CFO said margin flat
Down INR32.18bn (USD340mn) QoQ from INR95.8bn at March 31
Subject to finalisation within one year
Executable within one year: stated as INR9.6 million in transcript, likely INR9.6bn

segments.name: Tega Consumables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3.96bn (+36% YoY); EBITDA before one-time INR1bn at 24.1% margin (+320bps). About 23% of group revenue. Part of Q4 orders were serviced in Q1, so growth is not a clean run-rate.

segments.name: Tega Equipment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR358mn vs INR643mn (-44% YoY) due to delayed customer clearances; EBITDA roughly breakeven on lower volumes and operating leverage. About 2% of group revenue.

segments.name: Molycop (one month, June 2026)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR12.9bn and adjusted EBITDA INR1.6bn (~13% margin, USD17.2mn); gross margin ~36%. Volume FY (12m to Jun-26) 1.204mt vs 1.223mt prior; 12m EBITDA USD191mn, up 11% from USD172mn.

guidance_outlook: Consumables long-term revenue CAGR guidance of about 15% maintained; management called it sustainable.
Consumables EBITDA margin of 20-23% annually cited in Q&A; management said freight and commodity cost pass-through has about a one-quarter lag.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to stay around 15% for the full year.
Molycop: 10-month period volume expected up about 5% and EBITDA up about 4% on comparable basis; margin expected broadly flat quarter to quarter.
Molycop: about USD20mn of synergies targeted over the next two to two and a half years (SG&A, operations, procurement, scale).
Cross-selling revenue ramp expected from Q3 to Q4 FY27; quantified guidance deferred by a couple of quarters.
FY27 finance cost about INR110-120bn... stated as INR110-120 crore for the full year; Molycop 10-month interest and principal about USD70mn.
Tega capex (excluding Molycop) about USD40mn for FY27 including Chile; Molycop 10-month capex about USD28mn, normalised about low USD30mn annually.
Molycop net debt expected to decline by year-end; group divestment of non-core land parcels to repay debt, with no material EBITDA impact.
capex_capacity: Chile plant: soft commissioning around January 2027 and commercial production around March 2027, subject to local regulatory approvals expected within a two-month window.
Tega capex excluding Molycop about USD40mn for FY27 including Chile.
Molycop 10-month capex about USD28mn; normalised annual capex in low USD30mn range, with expansion-related opportunities possibly lifting it to low-to-mid USD30mn over two years.
Molycop volumes: 1.204mt in 12 months to June 2026 vs 1.223mt prior year.
Freeport Indonesia Grasberg: blocks 2 and 3 at planned rates; full return to planned capacity targeted by end-CY2027. Cobra Panama restart discussions ongoing.
demand_pricing: Molycop: around 85% of contracts have steel-index-linked pricing, so revenue per ton moves with steel; management tracks per-ton margin rather than percentage margin.
Molycop states above 50% market share in core regions; largest volumes in South America, with North America, Australasia and growing Africa.
Copper above USD14,000/t and gold around USD4,400/oz cited as supportive of mining investment.
Management says it has faced Chinese competition in Latin America for decades and maintains leading position via lead times, local footprint and technical support.

Freight costs have risen; Tega passes through freight in contracts with a quarter lag; Molycop hedges ocean freight and passes through land costs linked to gas prices. No material deferment of shipments seen.
Equipment shortfall attributed to customer clearance delays rather than demand loss.
